text:
maria: heads up — eu-central1 GPU attaches trending down, lots of "attach timeout" errors starting ~00:45 UTC. I see cluster-gpu-provisioner backoffs. Graph: https://dash.redwood.internal/graphs/attach-latency?view=euc1 :warning:

ops-bot: [ALERT] node-provisioner: attach_fail_rate > 5% in eu-central1 — auto-created incident #INC-2026-542

arjun: is this correlated with disk io? any nvme SMART or iostat spikes?

maria: yes — correlates with janitor/ephemeral-cleaner runs that kicked at 00:44. Pasted iostat from a hot node:

```
avg-cpu:  %user %nice %sys %iowait %idle
       3.2    0.0    4.9    85.6   6.3
Device            r/s     w/s      rkB/s   wkB/s
nvme0n1         1200.5  10.1    245120  1024
nvme1n1         1300.3  8.8    312040   880
```

maria: dmesg shows "nvme nvme0: I/O 0 QID 7 timeout" and metadata writeback bursts. Also seeing kernel messages about long metadata sync stalls.

len: looking at control plane, network egress to telemetry collector spiked at same time — agents pushing large per-file metadata to central store. That plus heavy NVMe reads is saturating the node's PCIe and host NIC buffers causing kubelet heartbeats to delay.

sophie: immediate mitigation ideas: 1) throttle janitor concurrency, 2) pause new GPU scheduling into eu-central1 until we confirm, 3) reduce metadata push frequency. We should avoid a full cluster drain. :thumbsup:

arjun: agree. can we gate with a quick taint and reduce janitor concurrency via the control plane config?

maria: applying now. patching janitor to concurrency=2 and pausing GPU scheduling for the region. Commands I'm running:

```
curl -X PATCH "https://control.redwood/api/v1/config" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
 -d '{"janitor":{"concurrency":2,"burst_rate":0.1}}'

kubectl taint nodes -l region=eu-central1 gpu-provisioning=paused:NoSchedule
```

ben: good short-term plan. Long-term: we should add device-level QoS (nvme namespace throttling), change janitor to batch metadata pushes (bulk+backoff), and alter attach logic to fallback to a cold model-cache attach instead of blocking GPU attach. Also consider moving telemetry uploads off the fast path.

arjun: creating follow-up ticket INF-2483 to implement throttle, device QoS, and a canary rollout of slower scrub. Adding cost impact note — when nodes remain in attach backoff we see ~12% extra reserved GPU hours (based on last week).

maria: will monitor. I left scrub paused for 10m while we watch attach success rate. updating graphs now — https://dash.redwood.internal/graphs/attach-latency?view=euc1

ops-bot: incident INC-2026-542 updated: mitigations applied, monitoring.

maria: thanks all — followups in INF-2483 and I'll post a postmortem if the scrub change is the root cause. :eyes:
